description: Bank of family media agreement clauses — every clause on the child is matched by one on the parent. The pairing is mandatory and a test enforces it, because an agreement whose every clause falls on the child is not an agreement.

pairs.parent: No phones at the table — me included.
pairs.note: This is the clause the agreement gets tested on first: your child measures you against it at the very next meal.

pairs.child: My phone or tablet sleeps outside my bedroom.
pairs.parent: My phone sleeps outside the bedroom too.

pairs.child: I tell Mom or Dad if someone talks to me and it makes me feel weird.
pairs.parent: I listen without raising my voice, and I don't take the device away on the spot.
pairs.note: The most important clause in the whole product. If your child expects to lose the device, they will tell no one — and the clause on the parent is the price that makes the clause on the child possible.

pairs.child: I don't watch anything new until I tell them first.
pairs.parent: I sit with them the first time they watch something new — even if it's only two minutes.

pairs.child: When my time is up, I put the device down — no arguing.
pairs.parent: I put my phone down when it's time to play with them — no arguing.

pairs.child: No screens for the hour before bed.
pairs.parent: No screens for the hour before bed — mine included, where they can see.

pairs.child: I don't take anyone's picture without asking them.
pairs.parent: I don't post their pictures without asking them.

pairs.child: We go over the agreement every month, and I get to ask for a change.
pairs.parent: I go over it with them and listen when they ask for a change, and if I say no I give them the reason.
